chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Hawkins's decline: vodka, the beard and rumours
summary: Caldwell heard Hawkins was drinking two fifths a day and not eating; Charlie Holmes described him as an old man of the mountains.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, it is. His daughter is a secretary to where his body was laid out in 141st, St. Nicholas

[Baptist] funeral parlor. His daughter was working there at the same time, when he passed. But we were down there at the River Boat. That's when they gave this thing for Red Allen, and Louie Metcalf was in charge of it. So I went down with Jimmy Rushing, couple of us together, and so the girl came to me and said, Happy, said, why don't you go and see Hawk? I said, I can't catch up with him. She said, well, he always asking about you. I said, well, where is he living? I said, well, they told me one place, go there, and he's not there. She (Unintelligible) said, well, you should go and try to help him out.
I said, what seems to be his trouble? Said, he drinking two fifths of vodka every day.

Not eating -- so one day I said (unintelligible), I said, well, let me go down and see if I can find him. But he didn't stay there. So I was reading in the paper or the television schedule, and I saw where he would be on this program. So I said, oh, I got to get this one.

-- stay home, catch Hawk. So when they came on, he didn't come on. But -- well, this is funny. He didn't show. So next night I didn't bother to look at television that much. Then Charlie Holmes called me. He said, Hap, did you catch Hawk. I said, I tried to catch

him two nights before, but he was scheduled to appear and didn't. He said, well, perhaps you should be glad you didn't catch him. I said, why, Charlie? He said, man, you wouldn't know him. Said, he came out there, and said, his whiskers was way down to his navel, said, looked like old man of the mountains. I said, Charlie, you got to be kidding. Says, no, Hap. Looked like old man of the mountains.
I said, well, I'm a son of a gun.
I said, gee whiz, I said, that don't sound right. But you hear so many different fantastic tales, you just listen and find out -- one say this. One say that. One saying the other. (Unintelligible)

Chick was over in Europe. (Unintelligible), hell, he been in Europe way up (unintelligible) for a good while. Said, but this gal, so and so, so and so. Oh, man, said, now, that don't mean nothing, but, said, you hear so many stories of -- I just put it to rest. And --
